newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania and JP Morgan sign $75 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania and JP Morgan sign $75 mln loan.

text.p: Lithuania signed a $75 million syndicated loan led by U.S. investment bank J.P. Morgan and involving 22 banks.
The loan was priced at Libor +2.25 basis points and matures in one year and one day. It follows a $33 million syndicated facility signed in April, priced at Libor +2.50 bp.
Bankers said the loan showed international confidence in Lithuania and that its cost of borrowing should fall further.
"The margin should continue to decrease if the republic chooses to return to the international banking market," J.P. Morgan vice-president Fergus Elder told a news conference.
Lithuania has tapped international markets several times, although it has been branded as the slowest reformer of the Baltic states since quitting the former Soviet Union in 1991.
It is also still recovering from a banking crisis that broke last year. The loan comes as the ruling Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP) is facing defeat at elections in October.

"It is a sign of international confidence in Lithuania that the timetable of the election has not interfered with the country's access to the capital markets," said J.P. Morgan managing director Jean Falcon.
He said banks had actually offered to lend $95.5 million to Lithuania.
